subsetRule.title: Microsoft Graph API (curated subset: directory, files, mail, calendar, Teams, Planner)
subsetRule.note: This document is a curated subset of the full Microsoft Graph v1.0 OpenAPI (see upstream.yaml, the verbatim vendor file this was derived from). It covers the resource groups a Graph integration realistically reaches (users, groups, sites, drives/driveItems, applications, servicePrincipals, organization, directory objects/roles, domains, invitations, teams/teamwork/chats, planner, and contacts), restricted to paths at most 5 segments deep (entity plus one or two levels of relationship), plus the bare /me singleton (the signed-in user). That keeps common single-hop operations (e.g. a drive item's /content or /createUploadSession) while dropping Graph's deep, rarely-used relationship chains (analytics-of-analytics, nested OneNote pages, etc.). Every path, parameter, and schema below is copied verbatim from Microsoft's own spec, not authored; see source.json for the full rationale.

notes: Microsoft publishes the full Graph v1.0 surface as an OpenAPI 3.0 document (generated from their CSDL metadata by their own tooling, not by us) at microsoftgraph/msgraph-metadata, which makes this found-openapi, not converted. The verbatim upstream (upstream.yaml, 44 MB, hash-locked) is 18,094 operations / 5,367 schemas across every Microsoft 365 workload (Teams, SharePoint, Intune device management, security & compliance, identity governance, education, print, ...). openapi.json serves a curated coverage:subset derived mechanically from that file by the subsetRule above (src/subset.ts, applied by `pnpm specs convert msgraph`, so a re-fetch re-derives it; not hand-authored): every path whose top-level resource is one a Graph integration realistically reaches (users, groups, sites, drives/driveItems, applications, servicePrincipals, organization, directory objects/roles, domains, invitations, teams/teamwork/chats, planner, contacts), restricted to at most 5 path segments (entity plus one or two levels of relationship/action), plus the bare /me singleton (the signed-in user, which the mock/adaptor address directly rather than through /users/{id}). That keeps single-hop operations like a driveItem's /content or /createUploadSession while dropping Graph's deep, rarely-used relationship chains (nested OneNote pages, analytics-of-analytics, etc.). Every path/parameter/schema kept is copied byte-for-byte from Microsoft's document (1,781 paths, 2,677 operations, 1,112 schemas as of 2026-11-21) via a transitive $ref closure, not re-authored, so completeness is 'complete' rather than best-effort. Verified against ast.json: the adaptor's 6 HTTP operations (create, get, getDrive, getFolder, getFile, uploadFile) are all generic builders with no fixed path, and every endpoint their docs/source name as an example (/drives/{id}, /drives/{id}/items/{id}/children, /drives/{id}/items/{id}/content, /drives/{id}/items/{id}/createUploadSession, /sites/{id}/drive, /groups/{id}/drive, /applications) is present in the subset. Previously this adaptor's spec was a ~17-endpoint hand-picked stub, the exact 'focused subset' anti-pattern AGENTS.md warns against; this replaces it with a real vendor document narrowed by a documented, mechanical rule instead of by guessing at adaptor usage. Left out: Intune/device management, security & compliance, identity governance, education, print, reports, and most of onenote/todo/presence, all real Graph resources the adaptor's generic builders could reach but that no realistic OpenFn workflow targets; a future pass could widen the depth/tag allowlist if that changes.
